cases.a: A low-cost old feature-phone was satisfactory for basic calls/texts but was increasingly embarrassing in social settings, and prepaid renewal became burdensome.
cases.path_y: Retain inexpensive pay-as-you-go Samsung; defer contract and avoid pressured phone stores.
cases.baseline: Low monthly spend and familiar calling/texting, but social discomfort and account frictions.
cases.tipping: A late-March night out called attention to the phone, followed by a free morning to research independently.
cases.path_x: Selected iPhone through existing carrier after comparing alternatives and negotiating away upfront handset cost.
cases.desired_b: Use a socially acceptable, easy-to-learn phone while retaining agency over the choice; later social/blogging use may be a consequence rather than prior motivation.
cases.reported_result: Purchase and some later social-feature use were reported; realized social acceptance and longer-term satisfaction not independently established.

pull.summary: Accessible network of iPhone users and perceived ease

anxiety.summary: Long contract, spending, sales pressure and fear of choosing badly

inertia.summary: The old phone already did necessary calls and texts at low cost

contradictions: The old phone was functionally sufficient, so a purely functional-improvement story is inadequate.
The participant reported later increased smartphone use but could not establish that this caused the original switch.
Facilitators' generalizations about 'causality' are not independent evidence of her internal motives.

cases.a: Travel storytelling felt constrained by phone and action-camera affordances, while serious photography seemed bulky and costly.
cases.path_y: Use mobile phone and GoPro selectively, retell travel stories orally, and avoid a full photo kit.
cases.baseline: Some photos and specialized rugged footage, but limited ability to show compelling everyday travel stories.
cases.tipping: Professional camera practice at a work shoot, travel disappointment and a later concrete occasion to film; exact causal contribution of seeing her sister is uncertain.
cases.path_x: Researched and selected a compact mirrorless Sony, sought expert advice, tried a retailer repeatedly and bought from another retailer when stock failures persisted.
cases.desired_b: Capture compelling, shareable travel and personal stories with professional-looking video without violating travel space limits.
cases.reported_result: The camera purchase is reported, and a later filming activity is discussed, but sustained long-term storytelling progress is not independently established.

push.summary: Previously missed recording opportunities and limitations of phone/GoPro

pull.summary: Hands-on camera experience and smaller mirrorless body with expert reassurance

anxiety.summary: Gear volume, price and choosing the wrong model

inertia.summary: Already owned phone/GoPro; learning and equipment burden delayed change

contradictions: The participant later doubted that seeing her sister was a decisive trigger; treating it as causal would be source overreach.
Multiple failed retailer purchases are a separate availability/fulfillment episode, not proof of product dissatisfaction.
Early post-purchase activity should not be silently counted as long-term Point B achievement.
